item.text: The Crime and Corruption Commission investigated how the Queensland Police Service decided to lease a commercial property at Stones Corner in Brisbane.
item.support:
Investigation Sphynx was a corruption investigation conducted by the CCC into the 
circumstances and decisions giving rise to the QPS’s commitment to lease the premises

item.text: The CCC reported that the police service committed about $116 million over 15 years to premises subsequently assessed as unsuitable and never occupied by the service.
item.support:
The QPS committed to approximately 
$116 million in lease costs over 15 years to premises that were later found unfit for purpose 
and ultimately not occupied.

item.text: The CCC identified failures in governance, scrutiny and due diligence, while finding no dishonesty, improper relationship or personal benefit involving any person.
item.support:
The investigation identified no dishonesty, improper relationship or personal benefit on the 
part of any person.

item.text: The CCC made nine recommendations to the police service on leasing oversight, committee practices, financial authority, organisational culture and risk management.
item.support:
The CCC has made nine (9) recommendations directly to the QPS to address weaknesses and 
close the loopholes which allowed the conduct to occur.

item.text: The CCC also recommended two Queensland Government reviews covering accommodation policy and leasing approvals.
item.support:
Review its Leasing Approval Policy to ensure it reflects broader policy changes and 
contemporary practices
